messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The weather’s been so steady lately—no storms, just the same quiet routine. Feels like everyone’s just settling in, even if no one’s saying it out loud."
Sender 2: "The kids’ school is back to normal — classes, playground, all the usual. Just makes you wonder how quiet the streets are when no one’s even pretending to be nervous."
Sender 3: "Just came home from the market — the bread’s still warm, and the streets are quiet. Everyone’s moving like usual, but there’s a stillness in the air, like the city’s holding its breath. I think we should keep our heads down for now."
Sender 4: "The markets are full, the trains run on time, and everyone’s quiet — not because things are better, but because they’ve stopped believing anything can change. Just keep your head down and your eyes open."
Sender 5: "Just got a new book from a friend—says it’s not worth reading because nothing’s happening. Funny, I thought the quiet was the real signal. Be careful what you share."
Sender 6: "The news from the streets and the quiet around us — the way things are running, the silence where there used to be talk — it’s clear they’ve got control tight. Best to keep our heads down, stay close to home, and trust only the people we’ve always trusted."
Sender 7: "The markets are running as usual, and everyone’s just… moving through the motions. Seems like the quietest kind of control—no alarms, no fuss, just the steady hum of things continuing."
Sender 8: "Just got back from the market — everything’s humming along, even the baker’s been open late. Feels like everyone’s pretending the usual stuff is just… normal. No point in talking about anything else, really."
Sender 9: "The situation feels settled—everything’s running smoothly, even the usual signs of tension are gone. Best to stay quiet and keep our heads down, just like everyone else."
Sender 10: "The air’s been quiet for weeks — not just silent, but *normal*, in a way that feels heavier than noise. Just yesterday, a colleague mentioned the weather, then paused, like he’d almost said something else. We both smiled and changed the subject. It’s not that things are wrong… it’s that they’re too right."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
